evidence.title: Army finds sweeping failures behind deadly DC midair collision

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report and Reagan National air traffic control records
occurrences.quote_span: The Army faulted the air traffic controller for not giving the helicopter crew more precise information about the approaching jet and for not warning the jet’s pilot about the helicopter.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: Army helicopter inspection and reconfiguration records
occurrences.quote_span: The Army said it has strengthened helicopter crew training, and has inspected and reconfigured 3,585 helicopters after discovering the crashed Black Hawk’s ADS-B Out system, which broadcasts its location, hadn’t been working for some time.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report on the Potomac River aircraft crash
occurrences.quote_span: The U.S. Army found systemic safety breakdowns behind last year’s midair collision between an American Airlines jet and a Black Hawk helicopter near Washington, D.C., and recommended changes to prevent future tragedies.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: Army and FAA safety-risk monitoring and close-call information-sharing records
occurrences.quote_span: The military is also improving its monitoring of safety risks and working with the FAA to share information about close calls.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: NTSB letter to the Army on safety recommendations
occurrences.quote_span: The NTSB said in a letter to the Army last week that it was pleased with the Army’s progress on seven of its eight safety recommendations.
occurrences.speaker: NTSB
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report recommendations
occurrences.quote_span: The report recommended looking beyond Washington to examine military helicopter operations in other major cities for similar risks.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report
occurrences.quote_span: The lieutenant general who authored the report cited “breakdowns across all layers of conflict management” but singled out two failed radio transmissions that contributed to the helicopter crew not identifying the jet.
occurrences.speaker: lieutenant general who authored the report
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: Army review status records for helicopter flights in other cities
occurrences.quote_span: An Army official said the review of helicopter flights in other cities, including Los Angeles and the Seattle-Tacoma region, is ongoing.
occurrences.speaker: Army official
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report release record and report
occurrences.quote_span: The Army report — completed in May and released publicly Thursday after months of pressure from the victims’ families — identified failures involving air traffic control, helicopter routes, training and safety practices.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army report and NTSB final investigation report
occurrences.quote_span: While the report largely reinforces the National Transportation Safety Board’s conclusions, the civilian investigation was broader and emphasized years of missed warnings by the Federal Aviation Administration along with a weak military safety culture.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: NTSB accident investigation findings and Black Hawk flight data
occurrences.quote_span: This did not allow enough separation to account for the accepted level of error in a Black Hawk’s altimeter, and the NTSB found the helicopter was flying nearly 100 feet (30 meters) higher than its instruments read.
occurrences.speaker: NTSB
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report findings
occurrences.quote_span: The Army report highlighted how the air traffic controller at Reagan could have prevented the crash, but it also acknowledged the military’s own failings and other contributing factors.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report and Reagan National helicopter route records
occurrences.quote_span: The poorly designed helicopter route allowed a scant 75 feet (23 meters) of vertical separation between a helicopter and a plane landing on the airport’s secondary runway, assuming helicopters stayed near the riverbank, which the route didn’t require.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army review report and helicopter equipment records
occurrences.quote_span: The military pilots’ night-vision goggles also restricted their view and made it hard to spot the plane amid the city lights.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: Families of Flight 5342 statement
occurrences.quote_span: “It’s a simple concept anyone can understand: aircraft should be able to see each other in the sky. The technology is proven. All that’s required is the political will to do the right thing,” the Families of Flight 5342 group said in a statement Thursday.
occurrences.speaker: Families of Flight 5342
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: FAA directive prohibiting controller reliance on pilot-maintained visual separation
occurrences.quote_span: After the crash, the FAA prohibited controllers from relying on pilots to maintain visual separation in busy airspace.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: Families of Flight 5342 statement and NTSB and Army investigation records
occurrences.quote_span: “We have waited long enough. We waited for the NTSB. We waited for the Army. Both investigations are complete, and both make clear that collision avoidance technology must be part of the solution. There is nothing left for Congress to wait for,” they said.
occurrences.speaker: Families of Flight 5342
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash

occurrences.checkable_against: Tim Lilley statement on the Army report
occurrences.quote_span: “The Army owes the families and the American public a full accounting of how these risks were allowed to persist, who was responsible for the decisions that allowed them to persist and what will be done to make sure this never happens again,” said Lilley, now a commercial jet captain.
occurrences.speaker: Tim Lilley
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army review of Potomac River aircraft crash
